I lost the election for class president—devastatingly, publicly. The humiliation forced me to examine why I'd wanted the title rather than the responsibility. That self-reflection led me to therapy, then to psychology studies, then to a career helping others through transformative moments. Losing gave me my calling.

CANDIDATE A:
I got into my first-choice graduate program and completed my degree along the path I'd planned. The work was hard but the trajectory matched my expectations. I'm now established in the field I'd always targeted.

CANDIDATE B:
My company's flagship product flopped spectacularly—we lost millions. While investigating why, we discovered an unexpected application in a different industry. That 'failure' became the foundation of a pivot worth ten times our original business. The crash was our launch.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:54"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both involve an initial failure leading to unexpected self-discovery and a new, successful direction."}
